result:
None of the three solutions gives the formula I believe is correct, so I am choosing the closest one.

I am working from my recollection of the Lavrauw–Storme–Van de Voorde result on small-weight codewords of projective geometric codes, which I have not re-derived: for n > 2, d(n,q) = q^{n-2}·d(2,q). A check at q = 2 is consistent with it. There d(2,2) = 4, and the complement of a hyperplane in PG(n,2) has 2^n points and meets every line in 0 or 2 points. So d(n,2) = 2^n = q^{n-2}·d(2,2).

- **Solution 1** gives q·d(2,q) − (q−1). For q = 2, n = 3 this is 7, below the weight-8 value that the q = 2 check gives. It also fails its own n = 2 sanity check, as the solution itself admits.
- **Solution 3** gives d(2,q)·(q+1)^{n−2}. For q = 2, n = 3 this is 12, not 8, so it is wrong.
- **Solution 2** gives q^n. This matches q^{n-2}·d(2,q) only when d(2,q) = q², which holds for q = 2 but not in general. For example, d(2,4) = 6 (a hyperoval), so the true value for q = 4, n = 3 would be 24, not 64. It is also not expressed in terms of d(2,q), so it is wrong in general.

Solution 2 is the only one that matches the correct formula in any case (q = 2), so it is the most likely to be right.

CHOICE: 2
